```artifact
Feature: Alarm Management and Event Logging

  Scenario: Event log includes all alarm occurrences
    Given the system is running
    When an alarm occurs
    Then the event log should include the alarm occurrence

  Scenario: Event log includes all alarm inhibitions
    Given the system is running
    And an alarm is active
    When the alarm is inhibited
    Then the event log should include the alarm inhibition

  Scenario: Event log includes all alarm cancellations
    Given the system is running
    And an alarm is active
    When the alarm is cancelled
    Then the event log should include the alarm cancellation

  Scenario: Event log includes all alarm resets
    Given the system is running
    And an alarm is active
    When the alarm is reset
    Then the event log should include the alarm reset

  Scenario: Event log includes all alarm acknowledgements
    Given the system is running
    And an alarm is active
    When the alarm is acknowledged
    Then the event log should include the alarm acknowledgement

  Scenario: GUI allows inhibiting alarms
    Given the system is running
    And an alarm is active
    When the user inhibits the alarm
    Then the alarm should be inhibited

  Scenario: GUI allows acknowledging alarms
    Given the system is running
    And an alarm is active
    When the user acknowledges the alarm
    Then the alarm should be acknowledged

  Scenario: GUI allows cancelling alarms
    Given the system is running
    And an alarm is active
    When the user cancels the alarm
    Then the alarm should be cancelled

  Scenario Outline: GUI allows setting an alarm on inspiration tidal volume above threshold
    Given the system is running
    When the user sets an alarm on inspiration tidal volume above <threshold> ml
    Then the alarm should be set with a threshold of <threshold> ml
    Examples:
      | threshold |
      | 80        |  # Normal value
      | 3000      |  # Normal value
      | 79        |  # Below lower bound
      | 3001      |  # Above upper bound
      | 85        |  # Edge value
      | 2995      |  # Edge value

  Scenario Outline: GUI has an alarm that fires if for 3 consecutive breaths PIP > user-specified threshold
    Given the system is running
    And the user sets a PIP alarm threshold of <threshold> cmH2O
    When the PIP exceeds <threshold> cmH2O for <breaths> consecutive breaths
    Then the PIP alarm should <fire_or_not>
    Examples:
      | threshold | breaths | fire_or_not |
      | 20        | 3       | fire        |  # Normal value
      | 20        | 2       | not fire    |  # Below threshold
      | 20        | 4       | fire        |  # Above threshold

  Scenario Outline: GUI has an alarm that fires if amount of leakage is > user-specified threshold
    Given the system is running
    And the user sets a leakage alarm threshold of <threshold> lpm
    When the leakage exceeds <threshold> lpm
    Then the leakage alarm should <fire_or_not>
    Examples:
      | threshold | fire_or_not |
      | 5         | fire        |  # Normal value
      | 150       | fire        |  # Normal value
      | 4         | not fire    |  # Below lower bound
      | 151       | not fire    |  # Above upper bound
      | 6         | fire        |  # Edge value
      | 149       | fire        |  # Edge value
```
